title: SWE-bench Verified No Longer Measures Frontier Coding Capabilities
description: Discussion on Hacker News about why the SWE-bench Verified benchmark no longer effectively measures frontier AI coding capabilities. Suggests benchmarks need updating as AI coding agents improve.
author: OpenAI / Hacker News

title: The West Forgot How to Make Things, Now It's Forgetting How to Code
description: Highly-discussed article (784 points on HN) about declining software engineering skills and the implications of increased reliance on AI coding tools. Community debate about whether AI is accelerating skill atrophy or transforming software development.
author: Tech Trenches / Hacker News

title: Using Coding Assistance Tools to Revive Abandoned Projects
description: Popular Hacker News discussion (306 points) about using AI coding assistants to revive and finish projects that were never going to be completed. Community sharing experiences of using AI tools to tackle old codebases and unfinished work.
author: Matthew Brunelle / Hacker News

title: Amateur Armed with ChatGPT Solves Erdős Problem
description: Viral story (554 points on HN) about an amateur mathematician using ChatGPT to solve an Erdős conjecture problem. Demonstrates how AI tools are enabling non-experts to make contributions to specialized fields.
author: Scientific American / Hacker News

title: OpenAI Privacy Filter Released
description: OpenAI released a privacy filter (255 points on HN), likely addressing concerns about data handling and privacy in AI systems. Community interest in privacy-preserving AI technologies.
author: OpenAI / Hacker News

title: Google to Invest Up to $40B in Anthropic
description: Google will invest $10B initially in Anthropic, with potential for up to $30B more if performance targets are met. Amazon also invested $5B on Monday and could commit up to an additional $20B. Massive capital inflows into AI safety-focused lab.
author: Rebecca Bellan / TechCrunch

title: OpenAI Releases GPT-5.5
description: OpenAI released GPT-5.5, described as the company's 'smartest and most intuitive' model yet. Said to be better at coding and more efficient, bringing company closer to an AI 'super app'.
author: Lucas Ropek / TechCrunch

title: ComfyUI Hits $500M Valuation
description: ComfyUI reached $500M valuation as creators seek more control over AI-generated media. Node-based UI for AI image generation gaining traction as users want greater control and customization.
author: Marina Temkin / TechCrunch

title: DeepSeek V4—almost on the frontier, a fraction of the price
description: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek released V4 preview models (V4-Pro and V4-Flash), positioning them as competitive with frontier models at significantly lower pricing points. This follows their V3.2 release from last December.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Code Quality Issues: Postmortem Analysis
description: Anthropic released a postmortem explaining why Claude Code was providing worse quality results over the past two months. Three separate bugs in the Claude Code harness caused issues, including a bug that kept clearing thinking from idle sessions every turn instead of just once, making Claude seem forgetful and repetitive.
author: Simon Willison

title: Serving the Bluesky For You Feed: SQLite at Scale
description: The Bluesky 'For You' feed serves ~72,000 users from a single Go process using SQLite on a gaming PC with 16 cores, 96GB RAM and 4TB NVMe. Total cost is $30/month. Shows how far SQLite can scale for real-time recommendation engines.
author: Simon Willison

title: SpaceX Working with Cursor, $60B Acquisition Option
description: SpaceX is working with AI coding startup Cursor and has an option to buy the company for $60 billion. Shows the strategic value of AI coding tools in major technology companies.
author: Tim Fernholz / TechCrunch

title: ArXiv Papers: Tool Attention Is All You Need for Scalable Agentic Workflows
description: Paper introducing 'Tool Attention Is All You Need: Dynamic Tool Gating and Lazy Schema Loading for Eliminating the MCP/Tools Tax in Scalable Agentic Workflows' - addresses efficiency challenges in AI agent tool use.
author: Anuj Sadani, Deepak Kumar / ArXiv

title: ArXiv Papers: Multi-Agent Empowerment and Emergence of Complex Behavior
description: Research on 'Multi-Agent Empowerment and Emergence of Complex Behavior in Groups' exploring how complex behaviors emerge in multi-agent systems through empowerment mechanisms.
author: Tristan Shah et al. / ArXiv

title: ArXiv Papers: Thinking with Reasoning Skills
description: Paper on 'Thinking with Reasoning Skills: Fewer Tokens, More Accuracy' presents techniques to improve LLM reasoning efficiency by using explicit reasoning skills, achieving better accuracy with fewer tokens.
author: Guangxiang Zhao et al. / ArXiv

title: ArXiv Papers: Agentic AI for Science Automation
description: Research on 'From Research Question to Scientific Workflow: Leveraging Agentic AI for Science Automation' explores how AI agents can automate scientific research workflows from hypothesis to results.
author: Bartosz Balis et al. / ArXiv

title: ArXiv Papers: Probabilistic Verification of Neural Networks
description: Paper on 'Probabilistic Verification of Neural Networks via Efficient Probabilistic Hull Generation' presents methods for verifying neural network behavior using probabilistic techniques.
author: Jingyang Li et al. / ArXiv

title: ArXiv Papers: Separable Expert Architecture for Privacy-Preserving LLM Personalization
description: Research on 'Separable Expert Architecture: Toward Privacy-Preserving LLM Personalization via Composable Adapters and Deletable User Proxies' presents techniques for personalizing LLMs while preserving user privacy.
author: Chris Schneider et al. / ArXiv

title: Claude Connecting Directly to Personal Apps
description: Anthropic announced Claude is connecting directly to personal apps like Spotify, Uber Eats, and TurboTax. This represents a move towards deeper integration of AI assistants into daily workflows and services.
author: The Verge

title: AI Threatens to Widen Inequality Gap
description: MIT professor Daron Acemoglu warns that AI will increase inequality between labor and capital. 'You require a certain degree of education, abstract and quantitative skills, familiarity with computers and coding in order to be using the models.' AI could help the rich get richer rather than democratize access.
author: Stevie Bonifield / The Verge

title: Extract PDF Text in Browser with LiteParse
description: Browser-based version of LlamaIndex's LiteParse tool for extracting text from PDFs entirely in the browser using the same libraries that run in Node.js. Shows the trend toward client-side AI processing.
author: Simon Willison

title: GPT-5.5 via Codex Backdoor API
description: Simon tested GPT-5.5 available in OpenAI Codex and rolling out to paid ChatGPT subscribers. Found it to be fast, effective and highly capable. 'It's hard to put into words what's good about it—I ask it to build things and it builds exactly what I ask for!'
author: Simon Willison

title: Qwen3.6-27B: Flagship-Level Coding in 27B Dense Model
description: Qwen claims their new 27B model delivers flagship-level agentic coding performance, surpassing their previous 397B MoE model. Available as a 16.8GB GGUF quantized version that runs locally with excellent results on code generation tasks.
author: Simon Willison

title: Firefox 150: Claude Mythos Found 271 Vulnerabilities
description: Mozilla's CTO Bobby Holley announced that Firefox 150 includes fixes for 271 vulnerabilities identified by Claude Mythos Preview. Called it a hopeful experience showing defenders have a chance to win decisively. Mythos is 'every bit as capable' as top security researchers.
author: Simon Willison

title: GitHub Copilot Individual Plans: Major Pricing Changes
description: GitHub updated Copilot pricing: tightening usage limits, pausing signups for individual plans, restricting Claude Opus 4.7 to $39/month 'Pro+' plan, and dropping previous Opus models. Reason: Agentic workflows fundamentally changed compute demands - long-running parallelized sessions consume far more resources than original plan structure supported.
author: Simon Willison

title: Google: 75% of All New Code is AI-Generated
description: Google CEO Sundar Pichai revealed that 75% of all Google's new code is AI-generated, up from 50% last fall. Google created a 'strike team' to improve AI models' coding capabilities and catch up to Anthropic, which writes 70-90% of its code with Claude Code as of February.
author: Stevie Bonifield / The Verge

title: Anthropic's Mythos Breach: Unauthorized Access
description: Unauthorized group gained access to Anthropic's exclusive cyber tool Mythos. The breach was described as 'humiliating' for the company. Mythos is Anthropic's most powerful cybersecurity-focused AI model.
author: Lucas Ropek / The Verge

title: ChatGPT Images 2.0: Where's the Raccoon with the Ham Radio?
description: Review of OpenAI's ChatGPT Images 2.0. Sam Altman said the leap from gpt-image-1 to gpt-image-2 was equivalent to jumping from GPT-3 to GPT-5. Simon tested it with increasingly absurd prompts including a raccoon with a ham radio hiding in crowds.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Opus 4.7 Token Count Analysis: 1.46x Increase
description: Analysis of Claude Opus 4.7's new tokenizer shows it uses 1.46x more tokens than 4.6 for the same content, effectively making it ~40% more expensive despite same pricing. For images, can be up to 3.01x more tokens due to higher resolution support (up to 2,576 pixels on long edge).
author: Simon Willison

title: Karpathy: LLMs as Thinking Tools and Knowledge Bases
description: Andrej Karpathy described using LLMs not just as answer machines but as thinking tools and for building personal knowledge bases for research topics. He noted concerns about 'starting to atrophy' his ability to write code manually as AI suddenly writes most of his code.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Amjad Masad: Replit at $9B Valuation with AI Handling Coding
description: Replit reached $9B valuation with AI handling coding, support, marketing, and workflows. Amjad Masad continues to advocate for AI disruption of coding jobs and democratization of software development for 1 billion developers.
author: Amjad Masad / Replit

title: Lex Fridman Podcast #490: State of AI in 2026
description: 4.5-hour comprehensive interview with Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka discussing the current state of AI progress, covering LLMs, AI coding, scaling laws, AI development in China, AI agents, GPUs, hardware, and AGI.
author: Lex Fridman
